headline: Finland's government has drafted a rule change that would put large data centers behind other users in the queue for grid connections.
score_reason: Pool 6 lowered by 2: the plan was already reported on 30 Sep 2026, and the pool headline reads as law when it is a government draft.
importance_line: Finnish electricity users could see less strain on prices and grid capacity, as the government intends, while data center developers would wait longer and have to arrange nearby power generation, but it is only a draft and the terms may change.
summary: TechRadar reports that Finland's government has drafted an amendment, meant to take effect on 1 Jan 2027, that would end first-come, first-served grid connections and place large data centers in lower-priority groups unless they meet extra requirements to generate power nearby and offer flexibility on demand; Data Center Dynamics already reported the plan on 30 Sep 2026. For qualifying projects, local generation would have to cover half of their expected yearly electricity use, and the first allocation under the new queue is planned for December 2027.
notes: Older news re-dated into the window: Data Center Dynamics ran the story on 30 Sep 2026 (headline and date seen in Google News; its page could not be opened). The pool headline reads as if the change is done, but TechRadar describes a draft. TechRadar does not name the ministry behind the draft. Not in our earlier reports or the last four pools; the editor may hold it as old news.
